READING PASSAGE 2

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 14–26, which are based on Reading Passage 2 below.

Urban Regeneration: an award-winning redevelopment project in Berlin

Paragraph A (Q14):

A Just over a kilometer south of Berlin's Potsdamer Platz, near the left bank of the Landwehr Canal, an extensive, triangular-shaped area of waste ground once separated the neighbourhoods of Kreuzberg to the east and Schöneberg to the west. Known as Gleisdreieck, meaning ‘triangle of rails’, it was formed by the intersection of different railway lines built in the mid-nineteenth century that entered Berlin from the south. Tracks, sheds and warehouses belonging to three old railway stations – Dresdner Bahnhof (1875-1882), Potsdamer Bahnhof (1838-1944) and Anhalter Bahnhof (1839-1952) – are situated on a raised area some twenty hectares in size, at a height of four metres above the surrounding ground level.

Paragraph B (Q15):

B As the railway infrastructure gradually ceased to be used, the whole area of Gleisdreieck became increasingly run down and abandoned, to the point of being used as a rubbish tip after 1945. Meanwhile, vegetation took over, turning it into a surprising, natural haven in the middle of built-up areas. The closeness of the wall which divided the city of Berlin between 1961 and 1990 also contributed to the fact that Gleisdreieck was for decades clearly identified as no-man’s-land. Only a station of the same name in Berlin’s underground railway system testified to its existence. Shortly before the fall of the Berlin Wall, however, the German Museum of Technology was established there, attracting large numbers of visitors and giving visibility to the site. More importantly, the unification of the formerly divided city gave the zone more centrality, at which point it became imperative to identify a purpose for it.

Paragraph C (Q16):

C After 2006, the State of Berlin put forward the proposal of converting Gleisdreieck into a large urban park that would integrate the different urban zones which converged there. The decades-long isolation of the site, which had formerly presented a problem, now represented an opportunity for joining the southern area of Potsdamer Platz with Kreuzberg and Schöneberg. The creation of the park would trigger one of the biggest urban expansions inside Berlin, all within a framework of multiple uses and social characteristics. It was necessary to stimulate the development of sixteen new hectares of local amenities that would be capable of integrating different generations and social groups in a sustainable way, and in harmony with nature. Following intense discussion with local proprietors and residents, the need to reconcile these goals with the conservation of railway heritage also emerged.

Paragraph D (Q17):

D Once the area had been subjected to a process of undergrowth clearance and decontamination, it was then organized around a combination of existing and added elements. The project as a whole was planned around a large central meadow, intersected from east to west by a concrete footpath, and from north to south by a pair of railway lines. Once a month, a train slowly travels along these lines from its parking shed to the German Museum of Technology. The concrete footpath, which is a continuation of one of the main Kreuzberg boulevards, starts in the east, bridges the four-metre difference in ground level by means of a stairway, and suddenly ends in the west on reaching the underground lines.

Paragraph E (Q18):

E North of the meadow, there is a large concrete slab with rounded edges. Being south-facing, this functions as a big sunny terrace, full of benches complete with footrests. In the south, the meadow overlooks Yorckstrasse, an underpass crossed by more than fifteen former railway bridges. To the east of the meadow there is quite a dense forest of pre-existing maples, oaks and birches, as well as newly planted trees of the same species. In this area, a couple of large metal frames each hold two swings. The edges of the park are finished with a collection of distinctive, functional spaces, for example a nursery, sports fields, concave surfaces for skateboards, stages for dancing, community gardens, or simply areas covered in gravel obtained from the site itself.

Paragraph F (Q19):

F Although initially the regeneration of Gleisdreieck Park was the subject of disagreement between those who were in favour of safeguarding the railway heritage and those who wanted to regenerate the adjacent neighbourhoods, it was opened to the public in September 2011. The heart of Berlin now has a new green lung, in which the atmosphere of various small, very different corners fits neatly into a large-scale, wide-ranging and robust general order. This has been possible precisely because the intervention was not limited to conserving industrial remains in order to promote railway history. And as a reminder of the six decades of human absence, during which nature took over, the park has been able to conserve to some extent the spirit of the non-place that preceded it.

questionGroups.bodyHtml:
Questions 14–19

Reading Passage 2 has six paragraphs, A–F.

Choose the correct heading for each paragraph from the list of headings below.

Drag a heading from the list and drop it onto the correct paragraph's answer box on the left.

List of Headings
i Objectives of the regeneration project
ii Architectural details of the station buildings
iii Features and facilities of the completed development
iv The remains of a railway system
v A positive evaluation of the finished project
vi A way of controlling development costs
vii Ways of crossing the site
viii Reasons why the area had become neglected

Questions 20–21

Choose TWO letters, A–E.

Which TWO reasons are given for the choice of Gleisdreieck as a site for a park?

Questions 22–23

Choose TWO letters, A–E.

Which TWO things did the State of Berlin hope to achieve with the Gleisdreieck development?

Questions 24–26

Complete the summary below.

Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.

In the middle of the new park is a 24 , where there is a path for pedestrians and two railway lines. A slow train uses these lines to make a regular journey between its base and a 25 . Benches have been provided on the north side, so that people can relax and enjoy the sunshine, and to the east is an area with mature trees of various kinds, as well as sets of swings. A range of sports and leisure areas are situated around the 26 of the site.

passageNotes.label: Paragraph A
passageNotes.text: 在柏林波茨坦广场以南约一公里处，靠近兰德韦尔运河左岸，一个广阔的三角形荒地区域曾将克罗伊茨贝格和舍恩贝格两个社区分隔开来。这片被称为 Gleisdreieck（意为‘铁路三角’）的区域，由19世纪中叶从南部进入柏林的不同铁路线交汇而成。属于三座旧火车站——德累斯顿火车站（1875-1882）、波茨坦火车站（1838-1944）和安哈尔特火车站（1839-1952）——的铁轨、棚屋和仓库坐落在一个面积约20公顷的高地上，比周围地面高出四米。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph B
passageNotes.text: 随着铁路基础设施逐渐停止使用，整个Gleisdreieck地区变得越来越破败和荒废，到1945年后甚至被用作垃圾倾倒场。与此同时，植被开始蔓延，将其变成了一个令人惊讶的、位于建成区中心的自然避风港。1961年至1990年间分割柏林城的柏林墙的邻近，也导致Gleisdreieck几十年来被明确地认定为无人区。只有柏林地铁系统中一个同名车站证明了它的存在。然而，在柏林墙倒塌前不久，德国技术博物馆在那里建立，吸引了大量游客，并使该地点获得了可见度。更重要的是，曾经分裂的城市的统一赋予了该区域更多的中心性，此时为其确定一个用途变得势在必行。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph C
passageNotes.text: 2006年后，柏林州提出了将Gleisdreieck改造成一个大型城市公园的建议，该公园将整合汇集于此的不同城市区域。该地块长达数十年的隔离，曾经是一个问题，现在则代表了一个将波茨坦广场南部区域与克罗伊茨贝格和舍恩贝格连接起来的机会。公园的创建将引发柏林内部最大的城市扩张之一，所有这些都在一个多功能和多社会特征的框架内。有必要刺激开发十六公顷新的地方便利设施，这些设施能够以可持续的方式和谐地与自然融合，整合不同代际和社会群体。经过与当地业主和居民的激烈讨论，还出现了需要将这些目标与铁路遗产保护相协调的需求。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph D
passageNotes.text: 该区域在经历了清理灌木丛和净化处理后，围绕着现有和新增元素的组合进行了组织。整个项目围绕一个大的中央草地规划，东西向被一条混凝土人行道横穿，南北向则被一对铁路线穿越。每月一次，一列火车会沿着这些线路从其停放棚缓慢行驶至德国技术博物馆。这条混凝土人行道是克罗伊茨贝格主要林荫大道之一的延续，从东边开始，通过一段楼梯跨越四米的地面高差，然后在西边到达地下线路时戛然而止。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph E
passageNotes.text: 草地的北面是一块带有圆角的巨大混凝土板。由于朝南，它成为了一个阳光充足的大露台，上面布满了配有脚凳的长椅。在南面，草地俯瞰着约克大街，这是一个由超过十五座旧铁路桥梁交叉的地下通道。草地的东面是一片相当茂密的森林，由原有的枫树、橡树和桦树以及新种植的同种树木组成。在这个区域，有几个大型金属框架，每个框架上挂着两个秋千。公园的边缘则由一系列独特的功能空间组成，例如一个苗圃、运动场、供滑板使用的凹面、舞蹈舞台、社区花园，或者仅仅是覆盖着从现场获取的砾石的区域。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph F
passageNotes.text: 尽管Gleisdreieck公园的再生最初在那些主张保护铁路遗产的人和那些希望再生邻近社区的人之间存在争议，但它于2011年9月向公众开放。柏林的心脏现在有了一个新的绿肺，其中各种小而迥异的角落巧妙地融入到一个大规模、广范围且稳健的总体秩序中。这之所以成为可能，正是因为干预措施并未局限于保护工业遗迹以推广铁路历史。并且，作为对人类缺席六十年、自然接管期间的提醒，公园得以在一定程度上保留了其前身——那个“非场所”的精神。

items.text:
（1）题目 14：（题干见题目区）
答案：iv（The remains of a railway system）
定位：正文 A 段，第2至3句
原文：Known as Gleisdreieck, meaning ‘triangle of rails’, it was formed by the intersection of different railway lines built in the mid-nineteenth century that entered Berlin from the south.
译文：这里被称为 Gleisdreieck，意为“铁路三角区”，由19世纪中叶从南面进入柏林的多条铁路线交汇形成。

解析：A 段围绕旧铁路线、轨道、车棚、仓库和三座旧车站展开，核心是遗留下来的铁路系统，因此匹配 The remains of a railway system。

（2）题目 15：（题干见题目区）
答案：viii（Reasons why the area had become neglected）
定位：正文 B 段，第1句
原文：As the railway infrastructure gradually ceased to be used, the whole area of Gleisdreieck became increasingly run down and abandoned, to the point of being used as a rubbish tip after 1945.
译文：随着铁路设施逐渐停用，整个 Gleisdreieck 日益破败并被遗弃，1945年后甚至被当作垃圾场。

解析：B 段依次解释铁路停用、柏林墙附近的隔离状态如何使此地长期破败荒废，故选 Reasons why the area had become neglected。

（3）题目 16：（题干见题目区）
答案：i（Objectives of the regeneration project）
定位：正文 C 段，第1句及后文目标说明
原文：the proposal of converting Gleisdreieck into a large urban park that would integrate the different urban zones which converged there.
译文：该提案计划把 Gleisdreieck 改造成一座大型城市公园，以连接在此交汇的不同城市区域。

解析：C 段集中列出项目目标：连接城区、创造公共设施、融合不同年龄与社会群体并保护铁路遗产，因此选 Objectives of the regeneration project。

（4）题目 17：（题干见题目区）
答案：vii（Ways of crossing the site）
定位：正文 D 段，第2句
原文：The project as a whole was planned around a large central meadow, intersected from east to west by a concrete footpath, and from north to south by a pair of railway lines.
译文：整个项目围绕一大片中央草地规划，一条混凝土步道东西贯穿，两条铁路线南北穿过。

解析：D 段说明步道、铁路、台阶以及与城市道路的连接，核心是穿越场地的不同方式，因此匹配 Ways of crossing the site。

（5）题目 18：（题干见题目区）
答案：iii（Features and facilities of the completed development）
定位：正文 E 段，末句
原文：The edges of the park are finished with a collection of distinctive, functional spaces, for example a nursery, sports fields, concave surfaces for skateboards, stages for dancing, community gardens
译文：公园边缘布置了一系列有特色的功能空间，例如托儿所、运动场、滑板场、舞台和社区花园。

解析：E 段逐项介绍阳光露台、树林、秋千及各类体育休闲设施，正是完工项目的 features and facilities。

（6）题目 19：（题干见题目区）
答案：v（A positive evaluation of the finished project）
定位：正文 F 段，第2句
原文：The heart of Berlin now has a new green lung, in which the atmosphere of various small, very different corners fits neatly into a large-scale, wide-ranging and robust general order.
译文：柏林中心如今拥有了一片新的“绿肺”，许多各具氛围的小角落和谐地融入宽广而稳固的整体格局。

解析：new green lung、fits neatly 等评价性语言肯定项目成果，整段是对完工公园的正面评价，故选 A positive evaluation of the finished project。

items.text:
（1）题目 20：（题干见题目区）
题目翻译：选择 Gleisdreieck 作为公园所在地的哪两个理由被提及？
答案：B（It contained a particular tourist attraction.）
定位：正文 B 段，倒数第2句
原文：Shortly before the fall of the Berlin Wall, however, the German Museum of Technology was established there, attracting large numbers of visitors and giving visibility to the site.
译文：然而，在柏林墙倒塌前不久，德国科技博物馆在此建立，吸引了大量游客，也提升了该地的知名度。

解析：German Museum of Technology 是场地内的 particular tourist attraction，attracting large numbers of visitors 说明它具有游客吸引力，所以选 B。

（2）题目 21：（题干见题目区）
题目翻译：选择 Gleisdreieck 作为公园所在地的哪两个理由被提及？
答案：C（It lay at the heart of the reunited city.）
定位：正文 B 段，末句
原文：the unification of the formerly divided city gave the zone more centrality, at which point it became imperative to identify a purpose for it.
译文：原本分裂的城市统一后，这一区域变得更具中心性，于是为它确定用途成为迫切任务。

解析：unification 对应 reunited city，more centrality 对应 lay at the heart，因此选 C。

（2）题目 23：（题干见题目区）
题目翻译：柏林州希望通过 Gleisdreieck 的开发实现哪两个目标？
答案：D（to preserve industrial remains）
定位：正文 C 段，末句
原文：the need to reconcile these goals with the conservation of railway heritage also emerged.
译文：同时也出现了把这些目标与铁路遗产保护协调起来的需要。

解析：conservation of railway heritage 对应 preserve industrial remains，所以选 D。

items.text:
（1）题目 24：In the middle of the new park is a ________, where there is a path for pedestrians and two railway lines. A slow train uses these lines to make a regular journey between its base and a ________. Benches have been provided on the north side, so that people can relax and enjoy the sunshine, and to the east is an area with mature trees of various kinds, as well as sets of swings. A range of sports and leisure areas are situated around the ________ of the site.
题目翻译：新公园中央是一片________，有步道和两条铁路线穿过。
答案：meadow
定位：正文 D 段，第2句
原文：The project as a whole was planned around a large central meadow, intersected from east to west by a concrete footpath, and from north to south by a pair of railway lines.
译文：整个项目围绕一大片中央草地规划，一条混凝土步道东西贯穿，两条铁路线南北穿过。

解析：题干 middle、path 和 two railway lines 与原句逐项对应；空格核心名词是 meadow。

（2）题目 25：In the middle of the new park is a ________, where there is a path for pedestrians and two railway lines. A slow train uses these lines to make a regular journey between its base and a ________. Benches have been provided on the north side, so that people can relax and enjoy the sunshine, and to the east is an area with mature trees of various kinds, as well as sets of swings. A range of sports and leisure areas are situated around the ________ of the site.
题目翻译：慢车定期在其基地与一座________之间往返。
答案：museum
定位：正文 D 段，第3句
原文：Once a month, a train slowly travels along these lines from its parking shed to the German Museum of Technology.
译文：每月一次，一列火车沿这些铁路线从停车棚缓慢驶往德国科技博物馆。

解析：base 改写 parking shed，终点是 German Museum of Technology；一词限制下填中心名词 museum。

（3）题目 26：In the middle of the new park is a ________, where there is a path for pedestrians and two railway lines. A slow train uses these lines to make a regular journey between its base and a ________. Benches have been provided on the north side, so that people can relax and enjoy the sunshine, and to the east is an area with mature trees of various kinds, as well as sets of swings. A range of sports and leisure areas are situated around the ________ of the site.
题目翻译：多种体育和休闲区域位于场地的________周围。
答案：edges
定位：正文 E 段，末句
原文：The edges of the park are finished with a collection of distinctive, functional spaces, for example a nursery, sports fields, concave surfaces for skateboards, stages for dancing, community gardens
译文：公园边缘布置了一系列有特色的功能空间，例如托儿所、运动场、滑板场、舞台和社区花园。

解析：sports and leisure areas 是原文功能空间的概括；它们位于公园的 edges，因此填复数 edges。
